notes: fix(#208, root cause): invalidate the per-tester OAuth token cache when credentials change (server-only; Bruno collection unchanged, OTST_V2.0.23). Real cause of the 'invalid credentials still ran all test cases' report: worker/access-token.js resolveAccessToken reused a still-valid CACHED token (cached_token_enc) regardless of whether the credentials had changed, so switching to invalid creds within the token TTL was never exercised (the token request is fetched server-side before Bruno and never appears in the report; fetchToken DOES throw on a real 401, so only the cache could have returned a token). Now a SHA-256 fingerprint of the credentials (profile + token_url + client_id + client_secret + scope + extra; secret hashed one-way, never stored) is saved with the cached token (new users.cached_token_cred_fp column) and the cache is reused only when the fingerprint matches; a credential change forces a re-fetch, so invalid credentials now throw -> the run is marked FAILED before Bruno with '[runner] Auth failed: HTTP 401 ...' in the Execution Log and no scenarios run. Schema + migration added (existing rows have NULL fp -> one safe re-fetch post-deploy). Server 1.11.68 -> 1.11.69; Bruno collection unchanged.

fix(#208 follow-up): fail-fast on an auth rejection (401/403) mid-flow. The 2026.95 fix stops a run when the OAuth token can't be obtained, but a bearer/static token that is present-but-expired/revoked can't be detected up-front (the server only decrypts it; it can't know it is dead without calling the provider), so the run proceeded and every request 401/403'd. library-bruno/auth.js gains checkAuthRejection(res, reqName), now called from the collection-level after-response (opencollection.yml) for every request: on the first 401/403 from a non-token request it logs a clear [ERROR] ('access/bearer token invalid or expired — update it in Profile > API Configuration'), records a FAILING 'Authentication accepted' assertion, and calls bru.runner.stopExecution() so the dead token does not cascade. Keyed strictly on 401/403 (a rejected credential) — 404/400 (wrong endpoint / bad request) and the token-acquisition request itself are left alone; the failing request is still recorded in the report. fix(#208): clear, fail-fast diagnostic when the access token cannot be obtained (invalid OAuth credentials). Previously each vendor 'Access Token' request only console.error'd on a missing access_token — no assertion, no message, no stop — so invalid credentials let the run continue and cascade into misleading 4xx errors on every downstream request (and the success path logged the token value, a leak). New library-bruno/auth.js handleAccessTokenResponse(res, {vendor}) is now called by all six 00-Access Token requests (Benerail/Bileto/Chaps/Paxone/Sqills/Turnit): on success it stores access_token and records a passing assertion WITHOUT logging the token; on failure (non-2xx or no token, trying access_token/accessToken/token) it emits a clear [ERROR] naming the likely cause (client_id/client_secret/scope/token URL), surfaces the provider's OAuth error/error_description, records a FAILING 'access token acquired' assertion, clears any stale token, and calls bru.runner.stopExecution() so the cascade never happens. feat(#258, Phase 1): surface OSDM requestedInformation. The provider can advertise, via the requestedInformation string on each offer part (AbstractOfferPart) and on the post-booking response (Booking), which passenger data must be populated before the next step (provisional booking -> confirmation) — a boolean expression over passengerSpecifications[i] paths (AND/OR/grouping, numeric or ANY index; a leaf is true when that attribute is set). fix(#188): booking failed with 400 'Invalid request content' because placeSelections.places[] did not match the OSDM SelectedPlace schema. SelectedPlace is additionalProperties:false and requires exactly { coachNumber, placeNumber, passengerRef } — all STRINGS, passengerRef SINGULAR. library-bruno/requestsBuilder.js placesForPassengers emitted passengerRefs (plural array) and potentially numeric coachNumber/placeNumber, so the vendor rejected the booking with 400. Now emits the conformant shape (one entry per passenger; coachNumber/placeNumber coerced to strings; passengerRef singular). The legacy single-place branch in accommodationAndPlaceSelection routes through the same helper. Additionally collectAvailablePlaces now reads the coach number from the OSDM Coach.number field (it was wrongly reading coachNumber, always undefined, so the picked place had no coach number and the required SelectedPlace.coachNumber was missing -> 400); coachNumber is kept only as a fallback for non-spec vendors. Fixes both 02. POST Create Booking and 09. POST Add Reservation (shared helper). Latent until #186 made the offer-time seat map work and places actually populate. fix(#186): plain seat scenarios sent an unresolved {{reservationId}} to the place map -> vendor 400. The place map (08/08b) and add-reservation (09) are keyed on a RESERVATION offer-part (resourceType=RESERVATION), but library-bruno/offers.js handleAccommodationAndPlaceSelection set reservationId/tripLegCoverage only on the COUCHETTE/BERTH branch. A plain seat scenario (SEATMAP_AT_OFFER / ADD_TO_BOOKING, accommodationSelection=NONE) never set them, so 08's URL contained the literal {{reservationId}} (%7B%7BreservationId%7D%7D) and the vendor rejected it with 400 (observed on Bileto). Now, for the seat path, when place selection is enabled and reservationId isn't already set, reservationId/reservationIds/tripLegCoverage are derived from the offer's first reservationOfferPart; offers with no reservation part log 'seat map not applicable'. opencollection.yml smart-run filter additionally skips any place-map request when reservationId is empty, so a malformed URL is never sent. Important: the earlier #182 finding ('Bileto serves no offer-time seat map') may have been based on this same malformed request - with reservationId now resolving, 08 sends a valid request and Bileto's real offer-context response can be observed (re-test recommended). The auth guards still checked localStorage.oscar_token (the legacy bearer-token model), but the verify-email flow only writes the httpOnly cookie + oscar_user — leaving oscar_token absent and bouncing the page back to / which bounced back to /welcome.html (visible 'blinking' on the welcome banner). Guards now use oscar_user as the session presence proxy; oscar_token is preserved for legacy Bearer-header fetches when present. Affects welcome.html, admin.html, compare.html, dashboard.html, profile.html, run-detail.html, run.html.
Existing administrator sessions were unaffected because they retained oscar_token in localStorage from before the cookie migration.
